messages.body_plain:
Hi all:

     I have become addicted to ggtree for a whole day, and find it a really fantastic tool.

I want to draw a tree with associated data, according to the facet_plot example:

https://guangchuangyu.github.io/2016/10/facet_plot-a-general-solution-to-associate-data-with-phylogenetic-tree/

However, the tip labels in my own data are very long, which cannot display completely in the left panel, if i use xlim, both of the panels will be scaled.

Please find the attachment plot and give me some advice.

Best wishes!

Lily

messages.subject_clean: what's legend group 0 mean
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Hope this email finds you well!

I am trying to use different colors to represent different species in a tree, in some of the trees I created(not all trees), I found a legend group named 0, I am pretty sure that there is no species' name called "0" in my case, and I find the same issue also appeared in an example on your "Tree Manipulation" web page.

May I ask where the group 0 coming from and what is the meaning of the corresponding tree branch that being marked by the color of group 0?

Thank you so much for your help!

Best,
Man

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-3idfLmOt_Bo/WmDowts3D1I/AAAAAAAAAAM/706RTUS5ztswh1PL1M7Hpb4tYCZUKqp7gCLcBGAs/s1600/Screen%2BShot%2B2018-01-18%2Bat%2B1.32.59%2BPM.png>

messages.subject: Re: what's legend group 0 mean
messages.subject_clean: what's legend group 0 mean
messages.body_plain:
The group 0 is reserved for any branches that are not belonging to any groups.

For legend, you can rename it or disable it.

Try :
ggtree(tree, aes(color=group)) + geom_tiplab() +
     scale_color_manual(values=c('black', rainbow_hcl(4)), breaks=names(cls)) + theme(legend.position="right")

It will display the legend without ‘group 0’.
​

messages.subject: Subsetting based on multiple bootstrap support values in newick file
messages.subject_clean: Subsetting based on multiple bootstrap support values in newick file
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I've used iqtree to build a large tree, and implemented the SH-aLRT and UFboot to compute node support values. The iqtree output stores these values as node labels with a slash separating the two values (SH-aLRT/UFboot). In the past, I have used something like "geom_point2(aes(subset=!isTip & label>0.7))" to mark nodes that are well supported on my tree, but now I would like to mark nodes that have above (or equal) 70 SH-aLRT value and above (or equal) 95 UFboot value. It is common now to combine multiple sources of node support using this notation, so I was surprised that I couldn't find an answer on google... my tree file is attached, any help would be appreciated.

Problem:

nodes are labeled X/Y, how can I use geom_point2 to mark a subset that has X>=70 & Y>=95

oops, geom_point2 should works. The geom_nodepoint was defined to set the aes(subset = !isTip).
